transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dana (CTO, BrightLeaf), Michael (Lead ML), Priya (Security), Sam (PM)

Summary:
Quick hosted API + console demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming behavior, param tuning (max_tokens/temperature/top_p), batching strategies, retry/backoff patterns and failure modes. Walked through Console Optimize suggestions briefly. Customer cares about latency SLOs (99p), cost/unit, and SOC2/KMS for PHI adjacent logs. Agreed pilot next steps.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and constraints (aws sagemaker + internal queuing)
- Live demo of streaming response and partial tokens
- Parameter impacts: temp, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences
- Batching & continuous batching tradeoffs for latency vs cost
- Retry/backoff patterns (429 handling, exponential backoff, idempotency keys)
- Console traces and cost/latency heatmaps, Optimize hints
- Security questions: KMS, VPC/private, audit logs, retention

Action items (readback included): see metadata

Transcript body:
00:00 Ava (Redwood AE): all right hello everyone thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood Inference, i'm joined by Liam who is our solutions engineer, how's everyone doing?
00:08 Dana (BrightLeaf): good thanks, excited to see the live run, we sent over the dataset earlier this morning.
00:12 Liam (Redwood SE): cool — i'll share my screen in a sec. quick context question, are you running inference today through sagemaker endpoints or a different gateway?
00:21 Michael: yeah it's mostly SageMaker + a small k8s pool; we do some ad-hoc batching in front of it, but the queuing adds jitter and we want less tail latency for short prompts.
00:33 Ava: perfect, that aligns with what we wanted to demo — hosted API fast path for low latency and some throughput knobs. we'll show streaming, then dig into batching tradeoffs and retries.
00:43 Liam: okay screen on — Console -> Models -> Live sandbox. note: we call the streaming chunk "delta frames" in the UI, you might see them as chunks.
00:55 Sam (Product PM): quick question before you start: our SLO is 99p under 300ms for sub-128 token completions, is that realistic?
01:04 Liam: short answer yes for hosted if you pick the right model tier and keep batching low, longer answer: it depends on model family, instance selection (A100 vs H100), and if you use prefix/kvcache hit rates. for tiny prompts cold start can matter.
01:20 Priya (Security): also we need to understand data handling — logs, KMS, and retention — we can't have raw PHI leave our VPC in some cases.
01:28 Ava: absolutely, we'll cover private deployment options and KMS integration. for hosted we have encryption at rest and in-transit, SOC 2 cert, and optional dedicated tenancy; for full on-prem we have a Private package.
01:40 Liam: starting the live gen. i'm sending a simple prompt: "Summarize patient intake note into three bullets". watch the streaming behaviour — you'll see the first partial token arrive quickly then the remainder.
01:51 Console (Liam): streaming chunk 1: "Patient presented"
01:55 Console (Liam): streaming chunk 2: "with complaints of chest pain..."
01:58 Michael: mm there's a small stutter between chunk 1 and 2, is that normal?
02:02 Liam: yes, a small gap can happen as the runtime flushes kv cache for context windows, but end-to-end latency is still lower than our typical SageMaker roundtrip. the gap size depends on batch size and model warmness.
02:18 Dana: can you demo what happens under higher concurrency?
02:22 Liam: sure i’ll bump concurrent requests to 40 and enable batching window 20ms.
02:28 Console (Liam): enabling continuous batching -> current QPS 40 -> latency 99p climbs to ~420ms for sub-128 tokens (demo).
02:40 Michael: so increasing batching buys throughput but hurts tail. what's the recommended pattern?
02:45 Liam: typical pattern: keep batching disabled or minimal for conversational short-turns — window 2-10ms; for bulk generations or embeddings raise windows to 50-200ms. Also use our Optimize tool which suggests batch size by analyzing token distribution.
02:59 Ava: want to show retry flow next — specifically 429s and transient failures.
03:04 Liam: yep. i'm going to simulate a throttled instance and show exponential backoff + jitter pattern.
03:10 Console (Liam): simulated 429 returned; client should implement exponential backoff starting at 100ms, double each retry, with jitter and stop after n attempts or fallback to cheaper model.
03:22 Michael: do you provide idempotency keys for safe retries? we've had duplicate charge concerns.
03:26 Liam: yes we advise idempotency keys for generation endpoints — the API accepts an idempotency token per request, and the client library will retry idempotently when you set it. also responses include Retry-After header for 429s in case immediate retry is not recommended.
03:40 Priya: what's retained in logs? are boilderplate prompts or PII scrubbed?
03:45 Ava: Hosted stores minimal metadata for billing; raw payload logs are optional. you can enable no-logs profiles or use Redwood Private where logs stay inside your VPC and integrate with your KMS/HSM. we'll send detailed security docs.
03:56 Liam: switching to parameter tuning — temperature, top_p, and max_tokens.
04:00 Console (Liam): demo prompt with temp 0.0 vs 0.8 — note deterministic vs creative outputs.
04:08 Michael: curious — do you surface token cost upfront per call?
04:11 Liam: yes Console shows token estimates and cost per request; Optimize gives suggestions to reduce token usage (stop tokens, truncation heuristics, and prefix caching).
04:20 Dana: can Optimize suggest quantization or model variant changes automatically?
04:24 Liam: it suggests model/quantization pairings based on latency and quality constraints — e.g., 4-bit quant with per-layer knobs for throughput sensitive workloads. you still want to run an eval to check quality delta.
04:36 Sam: about warmup — how do you recommend handling cold starts?
04:39 Liam: keep a small pool warm on Dedicated, or do a short synthetic traffic ramp before high-traffic periods. hosted tier uses prewarmed pools for enterprise customers with SLA.
04:50 Michael: bench question — can we run a 2-hour latency test using our sample payloads? we'd like to see 99p and median.
04:55 Ava: yes we'll provision a benchmark harness. Liam will run it and share results.
05:00 Liam: i'll just flag caveat that batch windowing can lead to throughput gains. i'll capture both sets: low-latency config (window 2ms) and throughput config (window 50ms).
05:10 Console (Liam): quick look at trace view — you can see per-token time breakdown, kernel stalls, and batching waits. this is useful to identify where the tail is introduced.
05:24 Priya: for compliance we need audit logs and SSO support. do you have SAML and RBAC?
05:30 Ava: yes SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs with retention controls. Private option gives you full control over where logs land and KMS keys.
05:40 Michael: are there client-side patterns to avoid duplicate completions on retry? we handle at-most-once semantics today.
05:44 Liam: idempotency keys help; for streaming you can use resumable streaming tokens (we provide a resume cursor) to avoid re-sending whole context. note that resumable streams are best-effort and depend on model cache consistency.
05:58 Dana: let's talk about failover — if the primary model is overloaded can you fallback to a cheaper model automatically?
06:03 Liam: yes you can set routing policies: prefer low-latency tier, fallback to cheaper model variant (quantized) or region fallback. Console shows routing rules per route.
06:14 Sam: how are requests billed when fallback occurs?
06:17 Ava: billing is by token + model tier used. if a fallback happens and completes on the cheaper model you are billed the cheaper model's per-token rate; if both are attempted there are options to avoid double billing via early-cancel semantics.
06:30 Michael: show us an example of the SDK retry snippet for exponential backoff?
06:32 Liam: (shares snippet) "retryPolicy: { initial:100, multiplier:2.0, maxRetries:5, jitter: true }" — also check idempotencyToken: uuidv4() in header.
06:45 Console (Liam): i'll run a simulated sequence with 3 retries then final success — watch the client logs.
06:52 ClientLogs (Liam): attempt 1 -> 429, wait ~120ms; attempt 2 -> 429, wait ~240ms; attempt 3 -> success; final latency = 780ms (includes retry time).
07:07 Michael: okay — that clarifies the user-visible latency when retries occur.
07:12 Dana: on data residency — we need US-only data processing for some workflows. how granular are regions?
07:17 Ava: we support region pinning by account and route; you can pin a route to us-east-1 and restrict model variants to that region. Private option supports on-prem.
07:27 Priya: does the hosted API ever share model internals or weights?
07:30 Liam: no, weights are never shared. models are managed by Redwood; you can bring-your-own-model in Private for air-gapped needs.
07:36 Sam: can we integrate our existing feature-store for context retrieval latency?
07:40 Liam: yes — you can do local retrieval then pass context as prompt, or use our caching layer to populate KV cache to reduce per-token overhead. note that large context windows increase kernel load.
07:52 Michael: any gotchas with stop sequences and tokenization that we should look for? we saw truncation mid-word before in another vendor.
07:57 Liam: be mindful of token boundaries and provide explicit stop sequences; the Console token viewer helps debug. also use our recommended encoding libs for deterministic token counts.
08:08 Dana: what's your standard pilot packaging? we want a small POC with 100k generated tokens/day equivalence to validate infra.
08:15 Ava: typical pilot: 4-week pilot, dedicated support hours, baseline benchmark, security review, and a proof-of-performance report. we'll size Dedicated if needed or keep hosted while you validate.
08:25 Michael: price sensitivity — do you have burst credits or committed discounts?
08:29 Ava: yes committed capacity for Dedicated with monthly/annual commits; hosted has usage tiers and volume discounts; we'll propose a pilot estimate in the pricing sheet.
08:38 Sam: small nit — do you provide client libraries for retry logic or examples for streaming resume?
08:42 Liam: yes clients (python/js) have built-in retry helpers, idempotency, and sample code for resumable streaming.
08:48 Priya: on encryption — do you support customer-managed KMS keys?
08:51 Ava: yes, you can provide a CMK for Private deployments, and for hosted enterprise we offer KMS integration and bring-your-own-key options.
08:58 Liam: quick demo end-to-end: low-latency config (window 2ms, concurrency 8) -> 99p 260ms, throughput config (window 50ms, concurrency 40) -> 99p 420ms but 5-8x throughput.
09:15 Dana: that's helpful tradeoff data. any final notes on observability?
09:18 Liam: Console has per-route latency heatmaps, per-token breakdowns, and cost attribution. Optimize flags are surfaced as recommendations in the Console.
09:26 Ava: recap of next steps — we'll send security docs, pricing, and run a benchmark next week; Liam will lead the benchmark. customer to share dataset and SLOs.
09:36 Michael: thanks, that sounds good.
09:39 Dana: appreciate the demo.
09:41 Ava: thanks everyone we'll follow up in email with the artifacts. bye.

End of transcript.
